headline: Sixteen German machinery builders confirm Saudi Food Manufacturing stands
deck: The German pavilion at Saudi Food Manufacturing is the best-documented exhibitor block of the month, down to hall and stand allocation.
excerpt: Sixteen German processing and packaging machinery builders have confirmed stands at Saudi Food Manufacturing in Jeddah, with hall and stand numbers already published.
content:
Saudi Food Manufacturing opens at the Jeddah Superdome on 27 September alongside The Saudi Food Show, and the German national pavilion has published a confirmed exhibitor roster down to stand numbers — a level of disclosure no other block at any Saudi show this month has matched.

The sixteen confirmed are ROVEMA, in packaging machinery at stand 17-M8; SOLLICH and Chocotech, both in chocolate and confectionery processing at 16-M8; Röders, confectionery machinery, at 16-L12; TRIMA Triebeser Maschinenbau, food processing, at 17-M12; HASSIA-REDATRON, beverage machinery, at 17-M9; NETZSCH España, processing and pumping, at 17-N6; Fuchs Food Solutions at 17-N1; FPT Middle East at 16-M1; Higel Kältetechnik, refrigeration, at 16-L8; Jokey, packaging containers, at 17-L9; ARI-Armaturen, industrial fittings, at 17-M1; Hörmann MEA, industrial doors, at 17-L16; Silikal, floor coatings, at 17-L1; SW-Paratus, automation, at 17-N5; and planemos, planning software, at 16-L3.

Read as a group rather than as a list, that is a complete factory. Processing and forming plant, packaging machinery, refrigeration, valves and fittings, automation, hygienic flooring, industrial doors and the planning software to lay it out — a Saudi food manufacturer walking that pavilion can specify most of a production line from suppliers standing within a few metres of each other. National pavilions are usually assembled that way deliberately, and it is a more effective sales structure than the same companies scattered across a hall.

The presence of Silikal and Hörmann alongside the machinery builders is the detail worth noticing. Hygienic floor coatings and industrial doors are not glamorous purchases, but they are where food plant design is actually constrained: a processing facility has to be cleanable to a standard that ordinary industrial construction does not meet, and the floor and the door openings are where that requirement is most often compromised.

The wider show is large. The organiser, ASP Events, puts the combined figures across both co-located exhibitions at more than 1,000 exhibitors from over 95 countries, with 100,000-plus products and 12,000 business meetings. An exhibitor directory header indicates roughly 205 exhibitors on the manufacturing side specifically, though the directory itself returned no records. MODON is strategic partner to both shows. Named processing and packaging exhibitors beyond the German pavilion include Multivac, JBT-Marel, Provisur, ITEC, ACME, Napco, Zultec and Anasia. A Swiss pavilion is confirmed but its roster is not published.

The show's structured content is built around a matchmaking programme and two awards schemes, which places the emphasis on scheduled buyer meetings rather than on a conference track.

National pavilions of this kind are typically assembled by a trade promotion agency working with an industry association, which is why they present as a coherent capability rather than as a set of unrelated stands. For a Saudi manufacturer evaluating a line, the arrangement allows several elements of the same specification to be compared in one visit.
author: Mo Qureshi
